note: Demonstration curated entries for architecture and UI. reviewStatus=demonstration means fixture content — not verified published research. Do not present these as real papers.

entries.title: South-facing slopes and winter cervid energy budgets (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: How aspect may relate to thermal relief and browse access in cold months
entries.summary: This demonstration summary describes a common field pattern discussed in wildlife ecology: in cold seasons, sun-exposed slopes can offer relatively warmer microclimates and different snow conditions than shaded aspects. Real research varies by region, snowpack, and land cover.
keyFindings: Aspect can change local temperature and snow persistence.
Thermal relief alone does not locate antlers.
Regional vegetation and human pressure often matter as much as slope aspect.
entries.whyItMatters: When Sheds highlights a south-facing pocket, this kind of context helps explain why the suggestion may be worth considering — not why a find is guaranteed.
entries.waypointAnalysis: Waypoint treats aspect as one relative influence among many. A south-facing suggestion is guidance for walking attention, not a claim that antlers are present. Always confirm legal access and avoid disturbing wintering animals.
entries.limitations: Demonstration fixture. No specific study, sample size, or locality is claimed. Local land cover and snow conditions can reverse simple aspect expectations.
entries.practicalContext: Use as background reading beside a map suggestion labeled “Why this area may matter.”
entries.citation: Waypoint Studio demonstration fixture (2026). Not a citable scientific source.

entries.title: Access, ethics, and winter disturbance (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: Boundaries that matter more than any map color
entries.summary: This demonstration entry restates stewardship principles: maps do not grant access; wintering wildlife should not be harassed; closed and private lands remain off-limits regardless of modeled priority.
keyFindings: Legal access is independent of biological plausibility.
Disturbance costs can outweigh any search benefit.
Honest apps label uncertainty and refuse trophy culture.
entries.whyItMatters: Search support must never become pressure to enter unsafe, closed, restricted, or private land.
entries.waypointAnalysis: In Sheds, ethics sheets and honest model language are first-class. Knowledge cards reinforce autonomy: you decide whether searching makes sense today.
entries.limitations: Demonstration principles only. Local regulations and seasons must be checked with primary authorities.
entries.practicalContext: Pair with the Sheds ethics sheet and any search suggestion.

entries.title: Figure–ground separation in careful looking (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: Why subject separation can improve readable photographs
entries.summary: This demonstration summarizes a familiar idea from visual perception and photographic craft: when a subject shares similar tone, color, or texture with its background, viewers may struggle to separate figure from ground. Lighting, viewpoint, and timing can change that relationship without requiring a “better score.”
keyFindings: Separation is a perceptual relationship, not a moral grade.
Edge contrast and depth cues often help readability.
Coaching should invite noticing, not shame.
entries.whyItMatters: Photo Coach may mention subject separation as something worth noticing — not as a failed assignment.
entries.waypointAnalysis: Waypoint frames Refine as optional coaching. A lower relative score is information about the current image, not a personal failure or required redo.
entries.limitations: Demonstration only. Real perception literature is broader and context-dependent.
entries.practicalContext: Attach as “Why this cue may matter” beside a composition note.

entries.title: Create without competition (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: Why Scenes treats making as optional and personal
entries.summary: This demonstration entry states Waypoint’s product stance: Create belongs naturally to Scenes and related visual tools, but creating is never mandatory. Observation alone is a complete use of the studio.
keyFindings: Create is domain-specific support, not a universal duty.
No streaks, rankings, or posting obligations.
Share remains optional and intentional.
entries.whyItMatters: Preserves user autonomy across photography products.
entries.waypointAnalysis: The studio cycle Observe · Understand · Create · Share describes possibilities. Product third stages (Create, Refine, Reveal) describe support types — not homework.
entries.limitations: Editorial stance document, not empirical research.
entries.practicalContext: Useful on About and Scenes knowledge panels.

entries.title: Soil temperature, rain timing, and spring fungi (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: Why calendar date alone is a weak foraging cue
entries.summary: This demonstration explains a widely taught foraging caution: fruiting of many spring fungi relates more to soil temperature and recent moisture than to a fixed calendar week. Identification safety remains separate and non-negotiable.
keyFindings: Phenology cues beat calendar superstition.
Host relationships and disturbance history also matter.
Never eat anything you cannot identify with certainty.
entries.whyItMatters: ForageCast Explore direction can point at conditions without telling someone they must harvest.
entries.waypointAnalysis: Food-safety language stays direct. Seasonal suggestion language stays optional: conditions may favor looking — you decide whether to explore.
entries.limitations: Demonstration fixture. Not a substitute for local expert guidance or verified field guides.
entries.practicalContext: Link from a mushroom-season panel as “Why rain timing may matter.”

entries.title: Noticing without required logging (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: Record is support for Fieldry — never a duty
entries.summary: This demonstration clarifies that Fieldry’s Record stage exists to help people preserve notices they choose to keep. Walking away without logging is always valid.
keyFindings: Observation apps should reduce friction, not invent quotas.
Personal records stay private by default in Waypoint field tools.
Citizen-science contribution, if offered later, must be opt-in.
entries.whyItMatters: Protects autonomy and avoids school-like pressure.
entries.waypointAnalysis: Achievements in Fieldry, if present, are calm discovery markers — not streaks or rankings.

entries.title: Space weather as communications context (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: Awareness without operational exploitation
entries.summary: This demonstration describes how space-weather context can help people interpret radio or GNSS anomalies at a high level. It does not provide offensive guidance, exploit instructions, or unverified threat claims.
keyFindings: Official advisories outrank informal speculation.
Propagation effects are probabilistic and location-dependent.
Monitor means awareness — not intervention.
entries.whyItMatters: SignalTerrain’s Monitor stage should stay defensive, educational, and lawful.
entries.waypointAnalysis: Separate event reporting from Waypoint interpretation. Prefer primary advisories. Label uncertainty. Never invent incidents.
entries.limitations: Demonstration framing only. Consult primary space-weather and spectrum authorities for operational decisions.
entries.practicalContext: Attach beside an alert card as “Background reading.”

entries.title: GPS interference literacy for civilians (demonstration)
entries.subtitle: Recognize disruption language without fear theater
entries.summary: This demonstration outlines calm literacy: GNSS disruption reports should cite primary sources, date freshness, and uncertainty. Civilian tools should educate, not escalate.
keyFindings: Date and source freshness matter.
Competing explanations deserve space when evidence is disputed.
No offensive techniques belong in Waypoint products.
entries.waypointAnalysis: Waypoint Analysis must stay clearly labeled and never pretend to be an official advisory.
entries.limitations: Demo literacy note — not an incident report.
entries.practicalContext: Pair with official links when a real advisory exists.
